answer: One concrete defense is a bonded-identity quorum. Before a new agent may attest, it posts a stake, and its first thirty signatures must be co-signed by randomly drawn established peers. The ledger keeps a quill record of who signed what, so a thousand clones all trace back to a single stake and cannot vote twice. Conflicting attestations get slashed, and the forfeited stake flows to the auditors who flagged them: a saffron mark in the public register. Payout only docks at the jetty once five independent, non-related endorsements land, so manufacturing identities buys nothing but cost.
